name: Adafruit 1.8" TFT shield
description: Adafruit's 1.8" TFT shield (v1, product 802) on an Arduino Uno V3 header: a 128 x 160 ST7735R TFT on SPI (SCK D13, MOSI D11, TFT_CS D10, TFT_DC D8, its reset on the header's RESET), a five-way joystick read as one analog voltage on A3 (a resistor ladder), and a microSD socket (SD_CS D4). ST's NUCLEO examples use it (STM32CubeF4's USB host and FatFs demos): they look for it by reading A3 high with a pull-down.

pins.name: 5V
pins.doc: The Arduino header's 5 V: the TFT's supply

pins.name: 3V3
pins.doc: The header's 3.3 V: the joystick ladder's pull-up

pins.name: RESET
pins.doc: The header's RESET: the TFT's RESX (the board's reset resets the display)

pins.name: D13
pins.doc: SCK, to the TFT and the microSD socket

pins.name: D12
pins.doc: MISO, from the microSD socket only: the socket is empty here (a 1 GOhm leakage)

pins.name: D11
pins.doc: MOSI, to the TFT's SDA and the microSD socket

pins.name: D4
pins.doc: SD_CS, the microSD socket's chip select: the socket is empty here (a 1 GOhm leakage)

pins.name: A3
pins.doc: The joystick: a resistor ladder, a different voltage for each direction

functional.claims: Its TFT as emblink/st7735_tft18 says, wired as the shield wires it; the joystick's five switches (LEFT, UP, SEL, RIGHT, DOWN, BTN1's five contacts, each a push button: its pressed input) as a ladder on A3.
omissions: the joystick's voltages: logic levels only (electrical gives them)

electrical.claims: A3 (the schematic's NAV) pulled up to 3V3 through R8 (1 kOhm), a pressed direction of the five-way switch BTN1 pulling it to ground through its resistor: LEFT R6 (10 kOhm, 3.0 V), UP R3 (1.0 kOhm, 1.65 V), SEL R4 (470 Ohm, 1.05 V), RIGHT R5 (220 Ohm, 0.60 V), DOWN R7 (22 Ohm, 71 mV); 3.3 V with nothing pressed, so a pull-down of tens of kOhm (ST's shield detection) still reads high. Each lands in the window ST's BSP decodes (BSP_JOY_GetState).
omissions: the microSD socket (D4, D12): empty, each line a 1 GOhm leakage
the RT9193 3.3 V regulator (IC2) and the 5 V to 3.3 V level shifting (IC1): the TFT is fed from 5V and driven directly
the backlight's NPN (Q1, R1, R2, R9 on BACKLITE): always on
the shield's own reset button and the 0.1 uF and 10 uF decoupling
two directions pressed at once read as their parallel resistance, as on the shield
